description: Lambda functions must have unique IAM execution roles

requirements.description: Two Lambda functions in the same template reference the same in-template execution role resource.
requirements.rationale: Sharing a single execution role across multiple Lambda functions violates the principle of least privilege: any permission needed by one function is automatically granted to the other, expanding the blast radius beyond what each function requires. AWS recommends a unique, narrowly-scoped execution role per function.

requirements.description: A Lambda function references an execution role that no other Lambda function in the template references.
requirements.rationale: A role used by exactly one Lambda function in scope satisfies the uniqueness requirement. No sharing is observed within the analyzable scope.

requirements.description: A Lambda function has no execution role configured at all.
requirements.rationale: This rule's purpose is to detect role sharing across Lambda functions. A missing role is a different security concern (handled by a separate rule that requires an execution role be specified). With no role identifier to compare, this rule cannot establish a sharing violation and should not flag.

requirements.description: Two Lambda functions reference distinct, separately-defined execution role resources, each with its own identity, even if their attached permissions or policy contents are identical.
requirements.rationale: User-resolved decision: identity-only semantics. The rule checks role identity (distinct IAM role resources/ARNs), not policy equivalence. Two separate role identities pass even if their policies happen to be the same.

requirements.description: A Lambda function references an external execution role identified by an ARN that is not defined in the template, and no other Lambda function in the template references the same ARN.
requirements.rationale: User-resolved decision: analyzable-scope semantics. The rule cannot see other templates or stacks that may share the role, so with no in-scope sharing observed, the function passes.

requirements.description: Two Lambda functions in the same template both reference the same external execution role identified by an out-of-template ARN.
requirements.rationale: Even though the role is defined externally, the in-scope evidence shows two Lambda functions sharing the same role ARN, which violates the unique-role-per-function requirement.

requirements.description: A Lambda function's execution role reference cannot be resolved to a concrete identifier at analysis time (e.g., it depends on a runtime parameter or unresolvable expression).
requirements.rationale: User-resolved decision: when a role identifier is unresolvable, equality with other roles cannot be determined. The rule must avoid false positives and pass.

requirements.description: Two Lambda functions in the same template each have unresolvable execution role references that may or may not refer to the same value.
requirements.rationale: User-resolved decision: equality between two unresolvable references cannot be established, so the rule cannot assert a sharing violation and should pass to avoid false positives.

requirements.description: Three or more Lambda functions in the same template all reference the same execution role.
requirements.rationale: Any sharing of a single execution role across multiple Lambda functions is a violation, regardless of how many functions share it. The rule should flag the assessed function whenever its role is also used by at least one other Lambda function in scope.

requirements.description: A template defines an execution role resource that is not referenced by any Lambda function (an unused or orphan role).
requirements.rationale: This rule evaluates Lambda functions, not IAM roles. An unreferenced role has no Lambda consumers and therefore no sharing violation. The rule has nothing to flag.

requirements.description: A single Lambda function in the template references an execution role, and no other resource of any kind references that role.
requirements.rationale: A role used by exactly one Lambda function and no other resource fully satisfies the uniqueness and dedicated-use requirement.
